correct_completion: she sent it to her manager.
full_sentence: Having finished the report early, she sent it to her manager.
acceptable_variants: she handed it in to her manager.
she was able to leave the office on time.

options.why_wrong: The verbless clause needs the main subject to be the one who finished the report. A sun cannot finish a report, so this creates a dangling modifier.
The subject 'it' (the report) cannot be the one who finished it, and 'late' contradicts 'early' in the stem.

options.text: she sent it to her manager.

options.why_wrong: This describes the report, but the verbless clause requires the main clause to state the action of the person who finished it.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses with an implied subject
explanation: A participle clause at the start of a sentence must share its implied subject with the main clause. Only the option with a person doing the action fits this rule.
